newsitem.title: USA: VLSI sees gross margins improving in 1997.
newsitem.headline: VLSI sees gross margins improving in 1997.

text.p: VLSI Technology Inc President and COO Richard Beyer said the company expects gross margins to gradually improve in each quarter of 1997 as revenue growth picks up steam.

"Gross margins for the first quarter are expected to be nominally better than prior guidance, expanding 1 to 1- 1/2 points from the 41.5 percent reported in the fourth quarter," he said in a presentation to a Robertson Stephens technology conference here.

Beyer said the company expects revenues in the first quarter to be in a "3-5 percent range down from the fourth quarter" and then to grow sequentially in the "mid-single digit range" in the second quarter befoe achieving stronger growth rates in the second half of the year.
Overall, the executive said he expects revenues for the full year to grow in the 10-15 percent range, "consistent with that which is expected in the industry."

The maker of high-performance custom integrated circuits aims to achieve gross margins in the 46 to 48 percent range in its ideal business model, with operating margins in the 20 to 23 percent range and return on equity of 20 percent or more, according to Beyer.
The company fell well short of this "success model" in 1996, with return on investment of just 4 percent, but is working towards achieving it, he said.
"The success model is not something we'll be achieving in 1997," he said, but added the company will be moving towards the model's objectives during the year.

"Going forward, we expect that we will continue to improve gross margins by about one percentage point per quarter," he said, adding this would bring it "by the end of the year to the lower range of our success model." sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400
